newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil dips $1, soft Mediterranean falters.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil dips $1, soft Mediterranean falters.

text.p: European gas oil prices eased $1 a tonne on Thursday due to poor demand and good supplies of mostly Russian material, traders said.
Rotterdam barges held at about 50 cents a tonne above June IPE for refinery material while stored product was about 50 cents under. June IPE was down $1 at $167.75 at 10127 GMT.
"German demand is non-existent at the moment and the Med is looking pretty soft as well," said a trader.
He valued 0.2 percent sulphur cargoes at just $1 a tonne above the IPE with 0.02 percent around $6 above.
In the Mediterranean a Turkish tender to buy gas oil was won at between $8 and $8.50 a tonne above the fob quotations. In the past this tender has often been won at $10 or more above.
Dealers said Italian material was offered both into Asia and northern Europe and saw no demand from Greece, which last year helped prop the summer gas oil market.
"You have to secure the outlets if you have Russian or Romanain oil," said a trader.
